title: Single Number III
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, in which exactly two elements appear only once and all the other elements appear exactly twice. Find the two elements that appear only once.
You can return the answer in ascending order. You must write an algorithm that runs in linear runtime complexity and uses only constant extra space.
inputFormat:
Line 1: an integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers in ascending order.
constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4
-2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1
Exactly two elements appear once.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
# XOR all, then split by a set bit
